title: Who counts as a plant?
question: Which living things count as plants, and how did their ancestors come to cover the land?
hook: Aristotle filed fungi under plants, yet today's definitions leave them out.
idea: Today's plants are mostly sunlight-fed organisms whose ancestors moved from water onto land.

beats.prompt: Aristotle's biology sorted living things into just plants and animals. Where would a fungus have gone?

choices.label: With the plants, since the plant kingdom held everything that was not an animal
In its own separate kingdom
choices.feedback: Tempting because fungi get their own kingdom today, but that came later.

choices.label: With the animals
choices.feedback: Tempting, but the old plant kingdom took every living thing that was not an animal.

beats.explain: The old plant kingdom included algae and fungi. Definitions have narrowed since and now exclude fungi and some algae.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in the history of plants on land in order.
items: An algal scum forms on land
Primitive land plants begin to diversify
beats.explain: The scum came about 1,200 million years ago, land plants about 450, diversification about 420 and flowering plants around 200.

beats.prompt: Sort each into the size group the sources place it in.
beats.explain: Plants in the broad sense run from single-celled desmids and picozoa to the largest trees.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: Plants are mostly photosynthetic, making sugars from sunlight.
A creature found living off a host takes its energy from that host.
So it cannot be a plant, since every plant makes its own sugars.
So it must belong to some other kingdom.
beats.explain: Plants are only predominantly photosynthetic. Some plants have evolved to be parasitic and take energy from other organisms.
